property_summary: For any input, the deployed contract's version() returns the major.minor.patch string equal to the constructor-declared version components (1,0,0); the mutant returns 1.0.1, breaking this for all inputs.

For any admissible input, after a successful call to setL1BlockValues by the depositor, c.number() equals the supplied _number; the mutant never updates number, so it violates this for inputs where _number differs from the initial value.

For any admissible inputs, after setL1BlockValues the stored number must equal the _number argument; the mutant stores _timestamp into number instead, so any call with _number != _timestamp breaks the rule.
After setL1BlockValues, the stored number equals the _number argument for any input; the mutant stores _number+1, breaking this for all inputs.

For any admissible input, a successful setL1BlockValues by the depositor sets c.number() equal to the _number parameter; the buggy version never writes _number to number, so number stays 0 and the rule fails.

After a depositor-authorized call to setL1BlockValues, the stored timestamp must always equal the _timestamp argument; the mutant never writes timestamp, so it violates this for (almost) every fuzzed input.

After any successful setL1BlockValues call by the depositor, c.timestamp() must equal the _timestamp argument; the mutant stores _number there instead, violating this for inputs where _number != _timestamp.

After any call to setL1BlockValues, the stored number equals the _number argument (timestamp equals _timestamp); the mutant overwrites number with _timestamp, so number() != _number whenever _number != _timestamp.

After any setL1BlockValues call from the depositor, c.basefee() must equal the _basefee argument supplied; the mutant never assigns basefee, so basefee() stays 0 and violates the rule for any nonzero _basefee.

A call from a non-depositor address successfully sets the L1 block values (timestamp equals the supplied parameter afterwards); the inverted-check mutant rejects non-depositors, so the call reverts and the rule fails.
Only the depositor account can change L1 block values, so a call from any other address must revert and leave number unchanged (0).
